Repeated validation maximization can overfit selection noise ([Cawley–Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). Recommended protocol: prespecify SASRec transition-residual ablations, hyperparameter ranges, checkpoint times, stopping rules and tie-breaking before trials. Give baseline and ablations equal GPU-second allocations and validation opportunities; equal epochs alone do not match compute. Log configurations, checkpoints, software versions and all training/diagnostic/failure costs against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42 and the 200-epoch environment default. Report performance versus cumulative compute, following [Dodge et al.](https://aclanthology.org/D19-1224/). Prespecification limits further selection flexibility; it cannot erase earlier adaptive search.

For uncertainty, retain paired binary hit indicators for identical users and candidates. Within each category, bootstrap the 200 users with replacement using identical resampled indices across models; average the four category differences equally and report a 95% interval, category deltas and discordant hit counts ([paired-bootstrap documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). One additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals condition on fixed training/candidate seeds and do not correct winner-selection bias. Keep the pinned 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42; sampled ranking can reverse full-catalog model comparisons ([Krichene–Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Reserve held-out evaluation for the frozen winner.

Recommended implementation checks: reload the exported predictor and compare raw scores from the training model’s evaluation path, candidate scoring and full-catalog scoring restricted to identical item IDs. Prespecify dtype-appropriate tolerances; record maximum errors and ranking disagreements. Cover residual enabled/disabled, category routing, padding/truncation, final-position selection, item indexing, masking and ties. Verify checkpoint reloads, batching and catalog chunking preserve scores and recommendations.
